summary: The change dedupes in-flight exact source-issue reads across live records that share a repository and issue identity, keeps retired parts and repository/installation scopes isolated, and still applies outcomes in record order; new fake-port regression tests cover sharing, failures, scope isolation and pass continuation. No actionable defect was found.

evidence: The maintenance read path now shares one in-flight exact issue GET per repository and issue identity within a pass; the new fake-port test shows 60 records over 4 source issues costing 4 reads per pass, reducing the per-record GitHub reads the task names as a likely cause.
Sharing is intentionally limited to live records: retired decomposition parts keep independent reads and repository or installation identities stay separate, both covered by fake-port tests.

The change is focused on the maintenance read path, leaves the thresholds in `src/host/throughput-watchdog-thresholds.ts` untouched, and does not alter review, CI, P0 or accounting gates; the issue outcome rule re-evaluates the median after 10 cycles.
